intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and street musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample freshly squeezed orange juice and local street food from the evening market stalls.

experiences.name: Overnight Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Bivouac Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a sky full of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake up for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes before trekking back.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina & Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the 16th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, the Saadian Tombs, and the vibrant spice, leather, and textile souks. Learn about centuries of Moroccan craftsmanship and trade history.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class with Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a local chef for an authentic hands-on cooking class. Start with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes including tagine, couscous, and bastilla. Enjoy your meal together at the end of the session.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Erg Chebbi Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a sandboard and carve down the towering rust-red dunes of Erg Chebbi for an adrenaline-pumping desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction for all skill levels. Combine with quad biking options nearby for extra thrills in the open desert landscape.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a shared petit taxi or airport bus (Alsa Bus Line 19, ~10 MAD) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour convenience store or a late-night street food stall near the hotel if available (~30–50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your carry-on accessible for easy check-in. Exchange a small amount of currency (MAD) at the airport for taxi fare. Confirm hotel has late check-in arranged. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the iconic Jemaa el-Fna Square in the heart of Marrakech Medina. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to see snake charmers, street musicians, and orange juice vendors. Stroll through the nearby Souks (markets) of spices, leather, and handcrafts. Entry is free — just watch your pockets and budget ~20–30 MAD for fresh-squeezed orange juice and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior view, free) and then head to the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry). A stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, mosaic tilework, and carved cedar ceilings. Walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD) for panoramic rooftop views of Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna Square at sunset when it transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Dozens of stalls serve harira soup, grilled meats, snails, and Moroccan sweets. Soak in the atmosphere with live Gnawa music performances — all free to watch.

meals.breakfast: Café de France on Jemaa el-Fna Square — mint tea, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), and amlou (almond-argan spread) for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food in the Souks — a bowl of harira soup and a kefta sandwich for ~40–60 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls — grilled brochettes, couscous, and fresh bread for ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are cobblestone. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 50% of the asking price. Keep a copy of your passport and small bills handy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Arrive early to beat crowds. Then walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its distinctive architecture, the Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated), and the covered market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Berber Museum (~200 MAD combined entry — splurge-worthy for culture lovers). The garden, once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, features electric-blue architecture and exotic plants. Alternatively, for a free option, visit the public Menara Gardens with its olive groves and reflecting pool (~30 min taxi ride).
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed hammam (traditional Moroccan bath) experience at a local hammam in the Medina. Budget hammams cost ~50–80 MAD and include a steam bath and kessa scrub — an authentic cultural experience. Afterward, browse the evening souks for souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a local café — khobz bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea for ~25–40 MAD
meals.lunch: Café Clock in the Medina — famous for camel burger or vegetarian tagine, ~80–100 MAD — a beloved budget cultural spot
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant (avoid tourist-facing restaurants on main square) — chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives for ~70–90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance or ask your hotel for a trusted local recommendation to avoid tourist-trap hammams. The Majorelle Garden sells tickets online — pre-book to save queuing time.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~6:00–7:00 AM) on a shared budget group tour to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley. Book a 3-day/2-night Sahara tour through a budget operator in Marrakech (~800–1,200 MAD per person including transport, accommodation, and camel ride). The scenic drive passes the High Atlas Mountains, Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m), and kasbahs en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou Ksar (~10 MAD entry) — an ancient fortified village used as a filming location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the mud-brick towers and walk the ramparts for panoramic views of the surrounding desert landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Continue driving through the Draa Valley, passing palmeries and traditional Berber villages. Arrive in the town of Ouarzazate or Zagora for overnight accommodation (included in tour package — basic guesthouse or riad). Enjoy a communal Moroccan dinner with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — bread, jam, and mint tea (~20–30 MAD or included in hotel)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant stop en route — tagine or couscous set menu for ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Included in tour package at guesthouse — traditional Moroccan communal dinner (harira, tagine, bread, tea)

day_by_day.notes: Pack layers — the Atlas Mountains can be cold even in March. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle. Confirm all inclusions with your tour operator before booking. Shared group tours are significantly cheaper than private tours.

day_by_day.morning: Continue the journey toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi sand dunes — the iconic Moroccan Sahara. En route, stop at the Todra Gorge, a dramatic canyon with 300m-high rose-colored rock walls. Take a short hike through the gorge floor (free, ~1 hour walk) and marvel at the geology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga by mid-afternoon. Check into a basic desert camp or guesthouse (included in tour). Rest and prepare for the sunset camel trek. Explore the small Berber village of Merzouga on foot and visit a local argan oil cooperative.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45–60 minute trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Watch the sun set over the golden sand sea — one of Morocco's most breathtaking experiences. Spend the night in a traditional desert camp (included in tour) with Berber music around a campfire under an extraordinary star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Included at guesthouse — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside café stop en route — kefta sandwich or tagine for ~50–70 MAD
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp — traditional Berber dinner under the stars (tagine, couscous, mint tea, dates)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a warm jacket and sleeping bag liner — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Protect your camera and phone from sand. Sunrise wake-up (~5:30 AM) is highly recommended for the next morning — ask your guide to wake you.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn to climb the nearest dune for a spectacular Sahara sunrise. The silence and colors of the desert at sunrise are unforgettable. Camel trek back to the camp, enjoy a simple Berber breakfast, then begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic southern route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Draa Valley palmeries — a lush oasis of date palms stretching for miles through an otherwise arid landscape. Visit the fortified village of Tamnougalt (small entry fee ~10 MAD) and interact with local Berber families. Continue driving through the Anti-Atlas mountains with dramatic lunar landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (~20:00–21:00). Drop off at Jemaa el-Fna or your hotel. Take a final evening stroll through the illuminated square, enjoy a last cup of Moroccan mint tea, and pick up any remaining souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp — Berber bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — tagine set menu at a local restaurant for ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — try a local Medina restaurant for a final tagine or pastilla (pigeon pie) for ~80–100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 9–10 hours with stops. Bring snacks and entertainment for the road. This is a long but scenic day — the varied Moroccan landscapes make it worthwhile. Confirm return drop-off point with your tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Marrakech. Visit any missed Medina spots or return to favorite areas. Browse the Mellah spice market for last-minute gifts — saffron, argan oil, and Ras el Hanout spice blend are excellent value souvenirs. Visit the rooftop café at Café des Épices for panoramic Medina views and a final mint tea (~30–40 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is 12:00 — request late checkout if your flight allows). Head to Marrakech Menara Airport via petit taxi (~50–70 MAD) or pre-booked airport transfer. Allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Morocco with incredible memories of the Medina, the High Atlas, and the Sahara Desert. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast — msemen pancakes with honey and argan oil at a local café for ~30–50 MAD, or included at hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Medina before heading to airport — a sandwich or bowl of harira for ~30–50 MAD
meals.dinner: At the airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Keep MAD cash for the taxi to the airport and any last purchases. Morocco does not allow MAD to be taken out of the country in large amounts — spend or exchange remaining dirhams before departure. Confirm flight check-in requirements with UA airline. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and hotel): ~2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–$350 USD) per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer or licensed petit taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the property. Grab a light late-night snack if available at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the hotel or room service upon arrival — keep it light after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress. Exchange some currency to Moroccan Dirham (MAD) at the airport for small expenses. Rest well — the adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, head into the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed Medina. Begin at the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers set the scene. Walk through the labyrinthine souks (spice market, leather goods, lanterns) with a local guide or self-guided map.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (mid-14th century Moroccan architecture, intricate tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings). Afterward, explore the Saadian Tombs, a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Stop by the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for a glimpse into Marrakech's multicultural history. Browse the Mellah market for local produce and preserved lemons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a spectacular open-air theatre — acrobats, musicians, henna artists, and dozens of food stalls fill the square. Enjoy the vibrant energy before heading to dinner in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy traditional Moroccan bread (khobz), msemen flatbread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near the spice souks — rooftop terrace with views over the Medina; try harira soup, kefta sandwich, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (budget-friendly, ~100–150 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — experience an authentic Moroccan feast: grilled merguez sausages, lamb skewers, snail soup, and Moroccan salads (~80–120 MAD per person) OR sit-down dinner at Restaurant Nomad in the Medina for modern Moroccan cuisine (~200–280 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) out of cultural respect. Bargaining in the souks is expected and part of the experience — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep small change handy for entrance fees and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden, a breathtaking 12-acre botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. The cobalt-blue villa housing the Berber Museum is a highlight. Arrive early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, visit the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum for a fascinating look at fashion and Moroccan artistic influence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century 'Palace of Wonders' that once rivaled the greatest palaces of Europe, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts. Explore the vast courtyard and underground passages. Then visit the Museum of Moroccan Arts (Dar Si Said) to see exquisite Berber jewelry, carpets, and woodwork. Take a relaxing walk through the Arset El Maach gardens nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Moroccan hammam (steam bath and scrub) for cultural immersion and relaxation — try Hammam de la Rose or a mid-range local hammam near the Medina. Afterward, enjoy a sunset rooftop drink with views over the Koutoubia Mosque minaret before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a Moroccan-style breakfast at a local café near the Medina — msemen with argan oil and honey, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Kif Kif or a local Medina restaurant — try a traditional tagine (chicken with preserved lemon and olives or lamb with prunes and almonds) with Moroccan bread (~150–200 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina — a lush garden setting with excellent Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion cuisine; try the pastilla (sweet-savory pigeon pie) or lamb shank tagine (~250–350 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets: ~70 MAD (garden only) or ~130 MAD with the Berber Museum. Book hammam in advance for the evening session. The YSL Museum is an additional ~100 MAD. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (18–24°C / 64–75°F) — ideal for garden visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from the hotel for a full-day excursion into the High Atlas Mountains via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass road. Stop at the fortified village of Ait Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Explore the ancient ksar (fortified village) with a local Berber guide, climbing to the top for panoramic views over the Draa Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley area) or explore traditional Berber villages in the foothills. Visit a local Berber family home for a cultural exchange and demonstration of traditional bread-baking or carpet weaving. Hike a short trail through the dramatic red-rock gorges of the Dades or Ourika Valley for an adventure element. Alternatively, visit the Telouet Kasbah — a crumbling 19th-century palace with stunning original tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by early evening (approximately 3–4 hour drive back). Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Medina or the hotel. This is a good evening for souvenir shopping or simply unwinding before the Sahara journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a local restaurant in Ait Benhaddou or a family-run guesthouse in the Atlas foothills — lamb tagine, Berber omelette, fresh salads, and mint tea (~120–180 MAD per person, often included in guided tour packages)
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Marrakech — try Al Fassia, a renowned Marrakchi restaurant run entirely by women, serving authentic Fassi cuisine; the seven-vegetable couscous is legendary (~300–400 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book this as a guided day tour through a reputable agency (approx. 400–600 MAD per person including transport) or hire a private driver. Start early (7:00–7:30 AM departure) to maximize time at sites. Bring a light jacket as the Atlas Mountains can be cooler than Marrakech. This is a long day — wear comfortable shoes for walking on uneven terrain at Ait Benhaddou.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the hotel and depart early for the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes) — approximately 8–9 hours by road, but the journey itself is spectacular. Travel through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass, passing through the Rose Valley and the Draa Valley palm groves. Stop at the stunning Todra Gorge — dramatic 300-meter-high rock walls with a shallow river running through — for a short walk and photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Tinghir and the Ziz Valley, passing through a seemingly endless corridor of date palm oases stretching for kilometers. Arrive in the Erfoud/Merzouga area by late afternoon. Check in to a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse near the Erg Chebbi dunes. After settling in, mount dromedary camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the dunes — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a traditional Berber desert camp nestled among the towering golden dunes of Erg Chebbi. Watch the sun set over the Sahara — the colors shifting from gold to deep orange to purple. After sunset, the Milky Way emerges in the pollution-free sky for extraordinary stargazing. Enjoy traditional Berber music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before checkout
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in the town of Ouarzazate or Tinghir — a local restaurant serving harira soup, kefta tagine, and fresh bread (~100–150 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — slow-cooked lamb or chicken tagine, Moroccan salads, couscous, and fresh Medjool dates served under the stars (~included in most mid-range camp packages, or ~200–300 MAD if separate)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — arrange a shared or private desert tour (2–3 days) through a reputable operator, which typically includes transport from Marrakech, accommodation at a mid-range desert camp (private tent with basic amenities), camel trek, and meals. Cost: approximately 800–1,500 MAD per person for a 2-night package. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C (41–50°F). Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for a magical dawn camel or quad bike ride to the highest dune crest to watch the sun rise over the Sahara — an unforgettable experience as the dunes glow in shades of amber and rose gold. After returning to camp, enjoy a traditional Berber breakfast. For adventure seekers, arrange a morning sandboarding session on the steep dunes of Erg Chebbi — boards are available to rent from local operators near the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small Berber village of Merzouga to interact with local nomadic families and learn about desert life. Optionally, visit a traditional nomad tent and learn about camel herding culture. Explore the edge of the dune sea on foot for photography. In the early afternoon, visit the Gnawa music village of Khamlia — a small community of West African descent who maintain ancient musical traditions; catch an impromptu performance if timing allows.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset over the Sahara from the top of a dune — bring a blanket and simply sit in silence as the desert colors shift. Return to camp for a farewell Berber dinner and a final evening of music and stargazing. Sleep in a comfortable desert tent with the sound of wind over the dunes.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber breakfast at camp — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, amlou (almond-argan spread), hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the camp or a local restaurant in Merzouga village — Berber omelette, vegetable tagine, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~80–120 MAD per person if not included in package)
meals.dinner: Final desert dinner at camp — slow-cooked mechoui (whole roasted lamb) or chicken tagine with preserved lemons, couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries for dessert (typically included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Quad biking in the dunes costs approximately 200–350 MAD per hour and is a thrilling way to explore. Sandboarding boards rent for ~50–80 MAD. The Khamlia village Gnawa music experience is free but a small donation to the musicians is appreciated. Protect your camera and phone from sand — bring a small zip-lock bag or protective case. This is the highlight day of the trip — embrace the silence and vastness of the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Wake for a final sunrise over the dunes before departing the desert camp. Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route through the southern oases. Stop at the ancient fortified granary of Agadir n'Ouzrou or the Tafilalt oasis region — the largest palm grove in Morocco — for a short walk and photos. Visit a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women along the route to see traditional argan oil production and purchase authentic products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by mid-to-late afternoon. If time allows before any late flights, visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (the exterior and gardens are accessible to non-Muslims) — the 12th-century minaret is the architectural inspiration for the Giralda in Seville and the Hassan Tower in Rabat. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — spices, leather goods, argan oil, and Berber rugs make excellent gifts. Return to the hotel area to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final celebratory dinner in Marrakech before any evening departures or a final night's rest. Reflect on an incredible week spanning ancient medinas, mountain kasbahs, and the infinite Sahara.

meals.breakfast: Final Berber breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch en route to Marrakech in Ouarzazate or Ait Benhaddou — try a local Moroccan restaurant for a final tagine or mechoui (~120–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Marrakech — treat yourself to a special experience at Dar Yacout or Comptoir Darna for a memorable final evening; enjoy classic Moroccan dishes like bastilla, lamb tagine, and orange blossom desserts with live music (~350–500 MAD per person) OR a more casual final meal at a rooftop restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight timing and arrange airport transport in advance. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for Marrakech Menara Airport check-in and security. If departing the next day, use this evening for relaxed exploration and a memorable final dinner. Keep some MAD for tips, last-minute purchases, and airport expenses. This 7-day itinerary covers approximately 1,200–1,500 km of Morocco's most spectacular landscapes — a truly balanced mix of culture, history, adventure, and desert magic.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged with a dedicated chauffeur holding a personalized name sign. Settle into Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a brief orientation from your personal concierge. Light unpacking and relaxation.

meals.breakfast: On flight or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome mezze platter and Moroccan pastilla bites arranged in-room by the resort upon arrival — paired with fresh-squeezed orange juice or a glass of chilled rosé

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort concierge is notified of your late arrival in advance. Request a turndown service with rose petals and traditional argan oil amenities. Keep Day 2 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort terrace. Afterward, take a private guided walk through the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding medina. Explore the labyrinthine souks with a knowledgeable local guide who will help you navigate the spice markets, leather tanneries (Chouara), and artisan workshops without the typical tourist overwhelm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private tour of the stunning Bahia Palace and the nearby El Badi Palace ruins — both UNESCO-recognized heritage sites offering a deep dive into Moroccan Saadian and Alaouite dynasty history. Your guide will provide rich historical context. Stop at a premium argan oil cooperative for a curated demonstration and shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking the medina and the Atlas Mountains silhouette. Followed by an exclusive dinner at a top-tier Marrakech riad restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous buffet at the resort featuring Moroccan msemen flatbreads, honey, fresh fruit, amlou (almond-argan spread), and made-to-order eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant in the medina — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb tagine with preserved lemon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai serving refined Moroccan-French fusion; reserve the private upper salon for an intimate experience

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the medina. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) out of cultural respect. Your guide can assist with any artisan purchases and ensure fair pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (MYSLM). Arrive early (before crowds) with a priority-access ticket arranged by your concierge. Stroll through the cobalt-blue botanical paradise, then explore the YSL museum's stunning exhibitions on fashion, art, and Morocco's influence on the designer's work.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive hammam and spa experience at a premium heritage riad spa — enjoy a traditional kessa scrub, rhassoul clay mask, and a full-body argan oil massage. Return to the resort refreshed. Optional: private calligraphy or Moroccan tile art (zellige) workshop arranged by the concierge for a hands-on cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner at your resort or a curated Fantasia show experience — a spectacular traditional Moroccan equestrian performance with live Gnawa music, followed by a multi-course feast under the stars.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — shakshuka, Moroccan crepes with honey and orange blossom, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café de France or a premium café near Majorelle — fresh salads, briouat pastries, and Moroccan mint tea
meals.dinner: Chez Ali Fantasia Dinner Show — a grand theatrical Moroccan feast with couscous, mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), and traditional pastilla; VIP seating arranged

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly. The hammam session should be booked at least 48 hours ahead through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 in a premium 4x4 luxury vehicle for the scenic drive toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorges. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas for panoramic photos and a warm Berber tea break at a scenic viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the ancient ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator). Enjoy a private guided tour with a local Berber historian. Lunch in the village. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses and Dadès Gorges, arriving at a luxury desert camp near Merzouga by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes at golden hour — a magical 45-minute ride to your exclusive private luxury desert camp. Watch the Saharan sunset paint the dunes in amber and crimson. Stargazing session with a private astronomer guide using high-powered telescopes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — energy-rich spread with dates, nuts, eggs, and Moroccan bread
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a family-run restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Moroccan salads, fresh bread
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner under the stars at your luxury desert camp — a curated Moroccan feast including harira soup, chicken bastilla, slow-cooked mechoui, and traditional sweets, accompanied by live Gnawa drumming and music

day_by_day.notes: The drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops. Dress in layers — the desert can be cool at night (March temperatures can drop to 8–12°C). Bring a scarf for the camel ride. Ensure your luxury camp (such as Scarabeo Camp or similar) is pre-booked with a private tent suite.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise hike to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most breathtaking experiences in all of Morocco. Watch the Sahara come alive in golden light. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast. Optional: quad biking or sandboarding on the dunes for an adrenaline rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Berber nomad family for an authentic cultural exchange — learn about traditional desert life, taste fresh camel milk, and see handwoven rugs and jewelry. Afterward, visit the ancient Ksar of Rissani, the historic capital of the Tafilalet region and ancestral home of the Alaouite dynasty. Explore the weekly souk if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the dunes once more, then a private Gnawa music and storytelling session around a bonfire at camp. Enjoy a traditional Moroccan hammam in the camp's private spa tent before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Saharan breakfast at camp — Berber bread baked in sand embers, honey, olive oil, goat cheese, fresh dates, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch prepared by the camp chef served in the dunes — mezze platters, grilled kefta skewers, couscous salad, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Exclusive multi-course dinner at the luxury desert camp — featuring Moroccan-French fusion cuisine, local wines or premium non-alcoholic beverages, and a live oud performance

day_by_day.notes: Bring high SPF sunscreen and UV-protective sunglasses for the dunes. Sandboarding equipment is provided by the camp. The cultural visit to the nomad family should be arranged respectfully through your camp guide.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at the spectacular Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls with a crystal-clear river running through. Short guided hike through the gorge with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Skoura Oasis — a lush palm grove with ancient kasbahs. Visit Kasbah Amridil, one of Morocco's most photographed and historic fortified homes. Enjoy a relaxed lunch in the oasis before continuing the drive back toward Marrakech, arriving by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort in Marrakech. Enjoy a restorative spa treatment or simply relax by the pool. Low-key evening with a private in-room dining experience or a quiet dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast — a warm, leisurely spread before the long drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium guesthouse restaurant in Skoura Oasis — slow-cooked lamb with dates, Moroccan salads, and fresh-squeezed juice in a serene garden setting
meals.dinner: In-room private dining at the resort — curated Moroccan tasting menu delivered by personal butler, featuring pastilla, tagine, and orange blossom crème brûlée for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 6–7 hours with stops. Comfortable travel attire recommended. Ensure your resort room is pre-prepared for a luxurious welcome back — request rose petal turndown and a chilled welcome drink.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Last-minute shopping in the medina souks for premium souvenirs: hand-stitched leather goods, saffron, argan oil, hand-painted ceramics, or a custom-made Berber carpet. Your concierge can arrange a private shopping guide to ensure authenticity and fair pricing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for checkout. Enjoy a final mint tea on the terrace. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport in a chauffeured vehicle. Arrive at the airport with ample time for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Carry with you the golden memories of the Sahara, the scent of spices, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final breakfast at the resort — a full spread of Moroccan and international options including fresh pastries, fruit platters, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a premium café near the souks — Moroccan mint tea, fresh-baked msemen, and a mezze plate; or at the resort before checkout
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport procedures. Duty-free at Marrakech airport offers quality Moroccan argan oil and saffron products. Ensure all purchased goods (especially carpets or antiques) comply with customs regulations. Tip your guides, drivers, and resort staff generously — it is customary and deeply appreciated in Moroccan culture.
